title: Tech Note: Testing if an XML Node Has Relatives
author: David Adams
featured_technology: DOM Get first child XML element / DOM Get parent XML element / DOM Get previous/next sibling XML element

historical_commentary.text: This note adds three small utility routines (DOM_NodeHasChildren, DOM_NodeHasAncestors, DOM_NodeHasSiblings) on top of 4D's native DOM XML API to safely test node relationships without triggering runtime errors, building on the reference-validation pattern from an earlier 2006 note. It is tightly coupled to 4D's classic DOM XML command set from the pre-v11 era; while the specific commands are legacy, the general technique of wrapping fragile low-level APIs with defensive, error-trapped helper functions remains a durable and still-applicable programming pattern.
related_updates: 4D has since added more modern XML/JSON handling (including native JSON support and later ORDA-based data access) reducing reliance on the classic DOM command set
The specific DOM XML commands referenced here remain in the 4D language for backward compatibility but are less commonly used for new development
